newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Flagging Don says to sell food units.
newsitem.headline: Flagging Don says to sell food units.

text.p: South African hotels firm Don Group Ltd said on Tuesday that it was negotiating to sell its food businesses and that future growth would be moderately paced.
The firm has recently issued statements warning its shareholders to use caution in dealing in its shares.

"We are negotiating with several interested organisations to take over our restaurant brands...we believe they will do better in a new food-related grouping," chairman Marc Wainer said in a statement.

The firm issued the statement in response to its falling share price, which has tumbled from as high as 400 cents at the beginning of the year to a closing price on Tuesday of 144 cents, down 14 cents on the day.

"Like everyone else in the hospitality business, some of our hotels are hurting because of the fall-off in occupancies...the fall in the share price is in line with what is happening in the sector and already discounts our results," Wainer said.
Wainer said the firm was experiencing the same difficulties as other hoteliers and was fundamentally healthy. "We're in the black and our assets far exceed our liabilities," he said.

But he added the firm's first fast expansion of growth was over. "Henceforth, expansion will be much more moderately paced. We'll go into areas where over-trading is less of a threat and and where our product fulfills a real need," Wainer said.
Don concentrates on apartment-style hotels, aimed mainly at business travellers.
The firm blames the tough environment in the hotels sector on South Africa's high crime rate, which has made headlines around the world.
"Business people flying into Johannesburg from other cities today try and do their business in a day and fly back home the same night rather than take risks," Wainer said.
